**Final finding: Compliant — no redline, no counterparty comment.**

No changes were made on this pass, because the verifier's own reasoning confirms the classification on every material point and identifies no defect to fix. Specifically, it agrees that: (i) there is no audit, inspection or records-examination right running against Client and no vendor access to Client systems; (ii) that absence puts us above the preferred position, so a redline is unwarranted; (iii) "missing" is inapposite for a rule whose purpose is to constrain a vendor-favourable right; and (iv) the failed `audit frequency limited` check is a heuristic artefact of there being no audit clause at all.

Evidence supporting the finding:

- **Nil searches:** "audit", "inspect", "records", "verify", "monitor", "books", "premises", "examination", "certif". "Usage" surfaces only § 2.34 downtime language and § 2.e.
- **Sections read in full:** § 5–6 (Compensation), § 8 (Client covenants), § 10 (Confidentiality) — the conventional homes for a usage or records audit. None contains a verification, examination or self-certification mechanic.
- **Rights that do exist favour us:** § 6 (documentation for charges plus right to contest) and § 2.e (real-time usage statistics and raw log files).

One caveat worth flagging for the reviewing team rather than the counterparty: the `audit frequency limited` check will continue to fail on this document no matter what a customer-side reviewer does, because it appears to look for frequency-limiting language and cannot distinguish "no audit clause" from "an unlimited audit clause." The only way to make it pass would be to draft a TrueLink audit right and then cap it — a net loss for Mortgage Logic.com. That is a check-tuning issue, not a drafting one.

Carried forward as awareness only: § 8.f permits TrueLink to implement technical mechanisms against spamming; this operates on its own Interface and belongs to the acceptable-use rule, not this one.
